physical_harm: Deceased died an unnatural death, subjected to cruelty and ill-treatment
number_of_offences: Three offences/counts charged, all finally upheld
premeditation_planning: Court found premeditation/planning as the death was caused by burns and harassment over dowry demands
motive: Dowry demands, particularly for material goods like television or cooler
key_evidence_accepted: Definite ocular, expert and documentary evidence to show that deceased died an unnatural death, she was subjected to cruelty and ill-treatment, there was demand of dowry of specific items like refrigerator, television and cooler and she died within seven years of her marriage.
witness_credibility: The statements of PW1 and PW2 were fully corroborated and found to be credible, with no contradiction or variation in their accounts.
post_offence_conduct: The accused prior to and immediately after the occurrence clearly shows that they were not innocent. Otherwise, there was no occasion for them to abscond after the body of the deceased was handed over to her relations.

legal_representation.accused: Dinesh Kumar Garg, Meha Aggarwal, Ashutosh Garg
legal_representation.state: S.S. Shamshery, Rahul Verma, Abhishek Atrey, Jatinder Kumar Bhatia

appeal_history.trial_court: Convicted under Section 304-B IPC and sentenced to life imprisonment

prosecution_argument: The prosecution case was that the husband, brother-in-law and mother-in-law of a woman burnt her to death after pouring kerosene on her, as she and her parents failed to satisfy their demands of dowry.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the deceased had died because of an accident of stove fire while cooking the food and that the accused had attempted to save the deceased, which would explain the injuries found on the accused's body.
legal_principle_applied: The Court applied the legal principle that the death of a woman caused by burns, bodily injury or otherwise than in normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage, subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or his family, in relation to a demand for dowry, is considered a 'dowry death' and the husband or relative is presumed to have caused her death.
precedent_relied_upon: Bansi Lal v. State of Haryana (2011) 11 SCC 359; Biswajit Halder alias Babu Halder & Anr. v. State of West Bengal (2008) 1SCC202; Meka Ramaswamy v. Dasari Mohan & Ors. AIR 1998 SC 774; Rajesh Tandon v. State of Punjab 1994 (1) SCALE 816; Kundula Bala Subrahmanyam & Anr. v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1993) 2 SCC 684; Asraf Ali v. State of Assam (2008) 16 SCC 328; Hemchand v. State of Haryana (1994) 6 SCC 727
sentencing_rationale: The Court held that the manner in which the offence was committed was brutal, committed for satisfaction of dowry demands, and the accused took up a false defence, thus the Court would not exercise judicial discretion to award a lesser sentence than life imprisonment.
judicial_aggravating_factors: The Court found that the manner in which the offence was committed was brutal, committed for satisfaction of dowry demands, and the accused took up a false defence.
